title: Rigidbody2D apply_impulse has inconsistent behaviour
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.5.1-stable, 4.6-stable (previous versions untested)

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.2.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Mobile) - integrated Apple M4 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M4 Pro (14 threads) - 64.00 GiB memory

### Issue description

The issue occurs on Rigidbody2D instances that have their mass set to a value greater than 1.0, when calling apply_impulse immediately after changing the process_mode from an initial value of DISABLED to INHERIT (or any other process mode that processes). The first call to apply_impulse appears to work as though mass is 1.0, subsequent calls of apply_impulse appear to work as expected.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a RigidBody2D instance to the scene with any shape.
2. Change the RigidBody2D mass to 2.
3. Set the RigidBody2D process mode to Disabled in the inspector.
4. In code, at a time of your choosing, set the RigidBody2D’s process_mode to INHERIT.
5. On the next line call `apply_impulse(Vector2(0.0, -800), Vector2.ZERO)`.
6. At a later point in time, call apply_impulse on the same RigidBody2D with the exact same values as used in the previous call.
7. Notice that the RigidBody2D does not react in the same way.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[rigid-body-2d-apply-impulse-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24951880/rigid-body-2d-apply-impulse-bug.zip)

The issue can be observed in the provided reproduction project:

1. Open the project.
2. Run the main scene.
3. Press space to apply an impulse to the godot icon sprite.
4. Press space again to see that the same impulse is not applied on subsequent calls.
